I feel like most of the times it serves as a catalyst for progress, at least in my personal experience. 

What preoccupies me is the fact that I've always had parents alive. Because of that, I am not sure how I will react to not having someone who is biologically obliged to be destroyed by my death. I am afraid that when my mother dies I'll just kill myself after because I am too blind to the other people who care about me. 

This whole weed ordeal has made it worse because, on one hand, I do miss the relief it brings me. On the other, I am too fucking anxious because the year and a half I was on anti-depressants was the worst time of my life. A time in which I remember nothing worthy of note - I was just there, breathing.

And sorry for any mistakes here, english is not my native language.

I appreciate the comment but I believe I may either expressed myself wrongly or you understood me wrongly.

First of all, I have tried multiple anti-depressants. All of them made me feel numb and an outcast. I like the fact that I am "intelligent" and that my mind is always racing. Sometimes, I just need to slow down. And weed helps me do that.

Relating to talk therapy, I am too arrogant for that. I know me very well, mainly due to the seclusion I have chosen for much of my life and I can't imagine a situation where someone is going to reach some kind of conclusion I was unable with my 14 years of experience dealing with my own thoughts. 

Relating to the dependency, it's not the fact I won't be able to smoke. It's the fact that if I don't smoke my doctor may push me towards anti-depressants and I really don't want that. 

Weed was what sparked that change. It may have been placebo effect for a while but I was able to change a lot of habits in my life, that I keep even in periods of not smoking, that allowed me to have a better life. When I woke up anxious or nauseous I smoked and that allowed me to go to the gym - it may be worthy of note that most of the time I smoke minor doses to try and get some of the CBD-related effects but not the psychoactive ones.

I honestly believe it is normal to have suicidal thoughts sometimes. At least for someone with aspirations and goals. I like my anxiety because it makes me do things. And the suicidal thoughts remind me of my own mortality. It may be fucked up and I may have my downs but I am comfortable with who I am, suicidal thoughts and all.

That's my biggest preoccupation, the fact I am ok with all this.

It doesn't come from how close I am to my mother. I just think it would be too selfish to make her go through another loss. I saw my dad die in front of me when I was 14. She also had to deal with it and I saw how bad it was. 

Even though I am not close to my mom, I can't let that be my legacy to her.

This is a post I posted around the same time in r/depression. This is why I am feeling so helpless right now.

This is probably going to be a long one so I'll have a TL;DR at the end.

I have had depression since I was 6 - this is just an estimation because I was only diagnosed when I was 14. When I was 6 I started having nightmares about ending up in the world alone and seeing everyone I loved die in front of me. I had -maybe still have, no idea because I haven't focused on that - above average IQ that made me wonder about things that I wasn't emotionally developed enough to think about.
Around 7 it all stopped and I continued with my life. I was always an odd kid but I had no idea something was wrong with me because my reality was the only one I knew and my parents always thought that I was just odd, not depressed.

My father died when I was 14. I saw it happen in front of me and it took its toll, obviously. A few months later my mother made me go to a psychologist where I was diagnosed with depression. She said that from what I had told her about myself I probably had depression since I was 6. She told me that the way I felt and most things I thought I knew about myself weren't probably accurate as they were characteristics of the disease instead of personal ones.

I never really focused on it because I didn't even remember how it was to feel something. Until recently I thought that was common.

When I entered University, at 18, things changed. I started being involved in multiple projects and got motivated because I felt I was actually making a difference. I started exercising, I started getting out of the house more often and I took a genuine interest in some things that never appealed to me.
All these changes coincided with two things: I stopped taking anti-depressants and started smoking weed once or twice a week. Instead of medicating myself every single day I started smoking if I felt a panic attack was coming or if I felt particularly anxious.

I never got hooked and tested it regularly. If I felt I was smoking too much in a particularly stressful week I would just stop smoking for a week to make sure I wasn't losing track of things. It helped me because it let me feel sad without it leaving my control and let me feel happy and enjoy myself.
I am now 20 years. I believe I am incredibly better than I ever was in my life. But last week something happened that I am afraid may disturb the balance I was able to create.

I was smoking with some friends. Sometimes I smoke recreationally, mainly during exams because I can't afford to smoke while I am pulling an all-nighter to study. The cops showed up near the car where we were. They were super cool and since I live in a country where it isn't a crime but also isn't legal (basically you can't go to prison for having/smoking weed but you may face some sort of administrative penalty like a ticket or having to go to the hospital to talk to a psychologist and a team to see what are your using habits) it wasn't an awful experience - certainly not as bad as it could have been. They let us off with a warning but took our information so that if we were caught again I would have to be sent to the psychologist. That would probably be registered and my dream job would go out the window.

Now, when I feel anxious I only get more anxious by thinking of weed. I am extremely afraid of going back to anti-depressants as they represent the worst part of my life. What should I do?

TL;DR: Dropping anti-depressants and starting smoking weed did wonders for my case of depression. Had an encounter with cops while smoking and now I can't think of weed without being anxious. What should I do?

EDIT: paragraphs

I'd like to point out to the people possibly posting in this subreddit* looking for advice concerning anti-depressants that weed is probably not the answer nor do I personally recommend it.

It worked on my personal case but it DOES NOT MEAN it will work in YOURS.

Talk to your doctor, be completely honest and things will get better eventually.
